strings.name: Rene Haas
strings.role: CEO of Arm and SoftBank Group International
strings.summary: Rene Haas has experience in semiconductor engineering, products and commercial management, including NVIDIA and leadership of Arm’s product business before becoming CEO. He helped lead Arm’s listing and expansion; processor architectures and chips are achievements of technical teams and partners.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Executive education and degrees, roles at distinct Arm and SoftBank entities, trading and IPO closing, and chip announcements, orders and future deliveries are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to Arm’s processor business, influencing mobile devices, data centers and the chip-licensing ecosystem.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: BS in electrical and electronics engineering from Clarkson University and completion of Stanford business school executive education; the latter is not an MBA.
strings.facts.f2.label: Career focus
strings.facts.f2.value: Progressed from applications engineering, products and commercial management to company leadership; he is not an original founder of the Arm architecture.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Managing a computing platform
strings.highlights.h1.text: Leads Arm’s product and business development across devices and data centers; team designs are not credited as his sole inventions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Beyond licensing
strings.highlights.h2.text: Under his leadership Arm expanded compute subsystems and its own silicon products; IP licensing alone no longer describes its 2026 strategy.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reports second-quarter progress
strings.timeline.t1.text: The company reports revenue growth for the quarter ended September 30. Initial AGI CPU commercial deliveries remain planned for Q4 FY2027; targets are not realized revenue.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Adds SoftBank Group International CEO role
strings.timeline.t2.text: Remains Arm CEO and director while coordinating SBGI semiconductor and AI portfolio companies; does not replace Masayoshi Son as SoftBank Group CEO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Arm announces AGI CPU
strings.timeline.t3.text: The company introduces its own CPU for AI data centers, working with Meta and other partners; announcement does not mean every deployment or commercial delivery is complete.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Arm ADSs begin trading
strings.timeline.t4.text: Trades on Nasdaq as ARM, with the offering closing September 18; the listing does not mean Haas personally sold all his interests.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Arm CEO and director
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeds Simon Segars with immediate effect; his predecessor provides short-term transition advice.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Leads Arm IP products
strings.timeline.t6.text: Becomes head of the IP product business, advancing its portfolio and software ecosystem investment.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Arm
strings.timeline.t7.text: Becomes vice president of strategic alliances, later taking commercial, sales and marketing responsibilities.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Takes NVIDIA computing-products leadership
strings.timeline.t8.text: Becomes vice president and general manager of computing products, spending about seven years at the company.
